panels.figure_caption: Depicting the histopathological features of the excised wall; highly cellular and invasive epithelial neoplasm organized in sheets (hematoxylin and eosin stain).
in_text_mentions: the excised wall revealed a highly cellular epithelial growth organized in papillae, lobules, sheets, and nests. The tumor displayed invasive characteristics, with polygonal cells exhibiting pleomorphic vesicular nuclei and moderate cytoplasm. Focal areas of keratin pearl formation and active mitosis were observed. The stroma showed significant necrosis and hyalinization, with a notable lymphocytic infiltrate in the interstitial spaces (Figure 5). Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated positive staining for pancytokeratin, focal positivity for CK, and negative staining for CK20 (Figure 6).
